 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 20.06.2011, passed by the tribunal, in MVC No.162/2009, questioning the liability fastened on the insurance company to pay compensation.
2. The factum of accident and the jeep got damaged in the accident are not disputed.
The disputed fact is that whether the driver of tipper was holding driving licence as on the date of accident or not.

3. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
4.
The tribunal while determining and awarding compensation has fastened liability on the appellant insurance company to pay compensation.
It is argued by the learned counsel for insurance company that the driver of tipper lorry was not holding driving licence as on the date of accident to drive the tipper lorry.
Ex.R.3 is the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13264 attested copy of driving licence of the tipper lorry furnished to the insurance company when the insurance company has issued notice to produce driving licence.
Ex.R.2 is the endorsement issued by the RTO, Raichur, stating that the driving licence No.2381/95-96 as per Ex.R.3 was not issued by the RTO, Raichur.
Therefore, as per Ex.R.2 endorsement the RTO, Raichur, has not issued the driving licence.
Respondent No.2 owner of tipper lorry or respondent No.1 have not produced the original of driving licence.

5. When the insurance company is successful in controverting the driving licence that Ex.R.3 driving licence is not the real driving licence, by producing Ex.R.2 endorsement issued by RTO, Raichur,
then the onus shifts on the claimant to prove that Ex.R.3 itself is the driving licence by producing the original driving licence.
When the onus shifts on respondent No.1, either respondent No.1 or respondent No.2 have to prove the driving licence but both of them have not discharged their burden.
The insurance NC: 2023:KHC-D:13264 company is able to establish that the driving licence Ex.R.3 is not issued by RTO, Raichur, as per Ex.R.2 document.

sentences.text: Therefore, the appellant insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of tipper lorry.
The owner of tipper lorry respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay compensation to the claimant.
Hence the appeal filed by the insurance company is liable to be allowed by modifying that respondent No.2 owner of tipper lorry alone shall pay compensation to the claimant.

7. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed.
ii) The judgment and award dated 20.06.2011, passed by the I Addl. MACT, Karwar,
in MVC No.162/2009, stands modified by holding that respondent No.2 owner of tipper lorry alone shall pay compensation to the claimant.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13264 iii) The appellant insurance company is exonerated from liability to pay compensation to the claimant as the liability is fastened on respondent No.2 owner of tipper lorry.
iv) The amount deposited by the insurance company shall be refunded to the appellant insurance company.
v) No order as to costs.
vi) Draw award accordingly.
